description.narrative: Palestinian women working in Israeli settlements are mostly women heading households and are suffering from challenging socio-economic, cultural, and political living conditions. As Palestinians, they endure the consequences of the Israeli occupation policies andpatriarchal and harmful social norms. Women workers are exposed to continuous violations such as cheap labor and are vulnerable tobeing exposed to different forms of sexual harassment and exploitation. These women work approximately 12 hours per day and are obliged to leave their children unattended. Those women leave for work in the early morning hours, jeopardizing the health and education of their children. In some situations, many women forced their daughters to drop out of school so that they take care of the household; which is an indirect form of gender-based violence. If not provided with new opportunities and alternative support their livelihoods, it is difficult for women workers to stop working in settlements since they do not have the required educational qualifications. Within this context, Oxfam and mother School Society will conduct a needs assessment on the reality, conditions and needs of the women workers in settlements by conducting interviews and focus groups and how to support them to live a dignified life. Target groups/beneficiaries: The project will target 45 Palestinian women working in Israeli Settlements Through these interventions we will reach to 5000 indirect target group that includes women’s headed households family members and community leaders and members.

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam Novib has been active in the Occupied Palestinian Territory/Israel (OPT/I) since 1982 and working with Palestinian refugees in Lebanon since the mid 1980s. It has built up a strong network of relationships with local NGOs and counts among its localcounterparts some of the largest and most professional NGOs in various sectors. It has accompanied these NGOs in their development from ad hoc volunteer groups to sizeable professional institutions with national outreach. At the same time the conceptualisation of the programme has evolved from three country programs in the early 1990s to a program for Palestinians in the Middle East (PME) working withPalestinians in OPT, Israel and Lebanon.
The programme has changed over the years with the establishment of the Palestinian Authority (PA) in the mid-1990s from a focus on support and service provision at a grassroots level and grassroots mobilization, to working towards influencing the establishment of the PA, its lawmaking and supporting building a democratic state # this involved supporting efforts of Palestinian civil society to build the basis for a democratic Palestinian state with room for civil participation, ensuring inclusion of vulnerable groups, refugees and women, and shaping its laws and systems. Oxfam Novib has also supported partners that are working on the provision of humanitarian assistance, response preparedness and conflict transformation. We have also supported partners in the provision of health services, access to quality education and gender justice.
